2026-12-17.title: Third Thursday of Annunciation
2026-12-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Those who have put on Christ
2026-12-17.verse: By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
theo: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Zechariah sings: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favourably on his people and redeemed them.” He sees God's ancient promises, to David, to Abraham, being fulfilled. Then he turns to his child: “And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High.” The song ends with an image of dawn: “the dawn from on high will break upon us.”

Paul tells the Galatians: “As many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ… you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.” The promises Zechariah sang about are ours through baptism. The Church sings his Benedictus every morning at dawn.

2026-12-17.prayer: Blessed are you, Lord God of Israel, for you have visited and redeemed your people. Let the dawn from on high shine on all in darkness and guide our feet into the way of peace. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana there is one table and one Bread for all. Whoever is clothed in Christ in baptism is welcome at his altar.

2026-12-17.question: Where do I need the dawn of Christ's light?

family.explain: Zechariah sang a song of thanks when John was born. He said Jesus would come like the morning sun to chase away darkness.
family.intention: We pray for people who are treated as less important because of their caste, colour or poverty.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we treat everyone as a child of God?”

pm.open: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has visited and redeemed his people. As we gather, clothe us with Christ and let the dawn from on high break upon us. Amen.
share: Paul says there is no longer Jew or Greek, slave or free (Galatians 3:28). What divisions still exist in my heart or community?
Zechariah sings of serving God without fear (Luke 1:74). What fear keeps me from serving God?
Where do I need the dawn from on high to break into my darkness?
pm.resp: Blessed be the Lord, who has visited his people.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home where all are one in Christ.
For those who suffer discrimination by caste, race or poverty.
For the newly baptised, that they may live clothed in Christ.
For those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, that the light of Christ may reach them.
For our families, that we may pray the Benedictus with grateful hearts.
pm.close: Lord God, by your tender mercy the dawn from on high is breaking upon us. Clothe us with Christ, make us one, and guide our feet into the way of peace. Amen.

illus: In an old parish in central Kerala, the parish priest invited the families of the colony, long kept at the edges, to carry the Christmas crib in the procession. Some parishioners grumbled. But that Christmas the whole parish sang together around one crib. All were one in Christ.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Galatians: in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith; as many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:26–27). Baptism is like putting on new clothes: Christ himself.

Then he says something revolutionary for his time: there is no longer Jew or Greek, slave or free, male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus (Galatians 3:28). In Christ the walls fall: caste, class, nationality, wealth. In Kerala, where divisions of caste and community have run deep, even in the Church, this word challenges us.

In the Gospel Zechariah, his tongue freed, sings the Benedictus: blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favourably on his people and redeemed them (Luke 1:68). The man who was silent for nine months now sings the history of salvation.

He sings of the oath sworn to Abraham, of deliverance from our enemies, so that we might serve him without fear, in holiness and righteousness all our days (Luke 1:73–75). Salvation frees us to serve without fear.

Then he turns to his tiny son: and you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways. And he ends with the dawn: by the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death (Luke 1:76–79).

Christmas is near: the dawn from on high. Let us pray the Benedictus each morning this week, perhaps as a family. And let us ask: whom do I treat as less than a child of God? In Christ, all are one. Amen.
kids: Children, Zechariah sang a beautiful song when John was born. Sing a song of thanks to God today!

intro: Zechariah's Benedictus and our baptismal inheritance.

points.h: He has raised up a mighty saviour
sub: God remembers his covenant with David.
The promise is fulfilled in Jesus.
q: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me; your throne shall be established forever.
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them. He has raised up a mighty savior for us in the house of his servant David.

sub: He gives knowledge of salvation by forgiveness.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me.
And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways, to give knowledge of salvation to his people by the forgiveness of their sins.

sub: Christ is the dawn from on high.
q: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; those who lived in a land of deep darkness—on them light has shined.
By the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high will break upon us, to give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
points.apply: Make peace with one person before Christmas.

concl: Let the dawn of Christ shine on us.
